source_extracts.claim: USPS will begin a fuel surcharge on package services starting January 2027, announced Oct 26, 2026
source_extracts.quote: The U.S. Postal Service will begin levying a fuel surcharge on various package shipping services starting in January 2027, the agency announced Monday.

source_extracts.claim: Applies to Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express, Parcel Select; domestic only
source_extracts.quote: The fuel fee will apply to USPS Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and Parcel Select shipments... The surcharge, which covers domestic shipments only

source_extracts.claim: Weekly updates from EIA diesel and jet fuel prices; percentage of base postage
source_extracts.quote: will update on a weekly basis based on diesel and jet fuel prices listed on the U.S. Energy Information Administration’s website. The Postal Service said the fuel surcharge will be calculated as a percentage of the base postage amount.

source_extracts.claim: Publishing lead times: 3-5 days diesel, 3-4 days jet fuel
source_extracts.quote: The specific percentage will be published three to five days prior to implementation for shipments in which diesel applies, and three to four days before implementation for jet fuel-applicable shipments.

source_extracts.claim: Fuel-type mapping: GA/Parcel Select = diesel, Priority/PM Express = jet fuel; base postage only, excludes extra services and nonstandard fees; retail and commercial incl. return services
source_extracts.quote: The surcharge will apply to both retail and commercial shipments using Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, USPS Ground Advantage and Parcel Select, including applicable return services. Ground Advantage and Parcel Select surcharges will be based on diesel prices, while Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express will use jet fuel prices reported by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA). The surcharge will be calculated as a percentage of base postage, excluding additional services and nonstandard fees.

source_extracts.claim: No starting percentages, formula, or min/max disclosed; rates may rise or fall weekly
source_extracts.quote: USPS has not disclosed the initial surcharge percentages, the formulas used to calculate them or whether weekly fluctuations will be subject to minimum or maximum limits. ... Rates could increase or decrease each week depending on fuel prices

source_extracts.claim: FAQ removed from PostalPro Oct 28, 2026, two days after publication, no explanation
source_extracts.quote: USPS has removed the Fuel Surcharge Implementation FAQ from its PostalPro website, just two days after publishing it. No explanation has been provided, and it's unclear whether the removal signals any changes to the planned January 2027 surcharge.

Q: What will happen to items that have the “old” surcharge amount (Retail /Commercial) — will they be postage due? A: Yes. Items should have the correct postage and fees paid for at the time of mailing.

source_extracts.claim: Temporary 8% increase: effective April 26, 2026, scheduled to expire Jan 17, 2027
source_extracts.quote: That temporary increase took effect April 26 and is currently scheduled to expire January 17, 2027

source_extracts.claim: USPS March 2026 framing: bridge to permanent mechanism; less than one-third of competitor fuel charges
source_extracts.quote: “this charge is less than one-third of what our competitors charge for fuel alone” and would “provide a necessary bridge to a permanent mechanism”

source_extracts.claim: Q3 FY2026: package revenue +7.7% YoY on -3.4% volume; $2.5B net loss
source_extracts.quote: The agency reported a $2.5 billion net loss in fiscal Q3 2026 ... even as Shipping and Packages revenue increased 7.7% despite a 3.4% decline in volume.

source_extracts.claim: FedEx and UPS levy their own fuel fees based on the same EIA diesel/jet prices
source_extracts.quote: these surcharges have contributed to elevated delivery prices for shippers throughout 2026 (FedEx/UPS fuel surcharge alignment)
